text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- State-run companies continue to pile up stocks, the paper says.
- Workers at the Avioane Craiova aircraft factory entered their third day of strike.
- Petrom RA oil authority signed accord with the National Agency for Mineral Resources to administer the oil blocks it operates.
- The new road taxes might affect freight transport, the paper says.

- Senate's legal commission approved a draft law allowing Romanians' access to their own files with the former communist Securitate secret police. The draft will also allow access to files of political personalities to allay suspicion that they cooperated with the Securitate.
- Romania expelled 18 illegal Turkish immigrants who tried to cross the border to Hungary on their way to the West.
- Health Minister Stefan Dragulescu might be sacked after recent scandal when a man was thrown from an ambulance and left to die in the street, the newspaper says.
- The main opposition Party of Social Democracy will back the ratification of the Romanian-Ukrainian treaty initialled last week in Kiev.
- Infanticide cases are on the rise across the country with mothers killing their new-born babies due to dropping living standards, the newspaper says.

- Border guards on Romania's southern border accuse Bulgarians and using explosives to fish across the Romanian River Dabube border. The guards said such fishing was a threat for passenger and freight traffic on the Danube.
- A planned bill on Romanians' access to their Securitate files, a special commission would issue certificates of Securitate collaborators. ($=7,092 lei)
